name: What happens if a backyard renovation changes drainage toward a neighbor?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a backyard renovation changes runoff toward a neighboring property?
mainEntity.text: What happens if a backyard renovation changes runoff toward a neighboring property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Backyard renovations should never create new runoff problems for adjacent homes. If grading, hardscape, or retaining walls change the way water flows, the design needs to be adjusted before the project is completed. The safer approach is to map existing drainage, identify low points, and design the site so water stays controlled on the property and exits at an approved point. In dense Los Angeles neighborhoods, even small slope changes can affect a neighboring lot. That is why drainage planning belongs at the beginning of the project, not after finishes are installed. If a contractor ignores drainage, homeowners risk future repair costs and neighbor conflict. A good renovation should improve both function and long-term site stability.
acceptedAnswer.description: If a renovation redirects runoff toward a neighboring property, the design should be corrected before construction is finalized. Drainage changes can create flooding, damage, and disputes, so the site plan should keep water on the property and direct it to approved drainage points.
